newsitem.title: USA: Fla. judge sees talks unlikely affecting case.
newsitem.headline: Fla. judge sees talks unlikely affecting case.

text.p: The Florida judge hearing a class action suit brought by flight attendants against the tobacco industry said Monday he did not expect the so-called "global" cigarette industry settlement talks to affect the trial.
"I don't intend to do anything yet with this because there isn't anything to do (yet). We will proceed as we are proceeding," Dade County Circuit Judge Robert Kaye said.

Kaye made his comments after a motion by Susan and Stanley Rosenblatt, attorneys for the plaintiffs in the case, that he issue an order that a settlement between government officials and tobacco companies not affect the class action suit, known as Broin vs Philip Morris Cos Inc.
He did not rule on the motion but indicated that he did not feel at this moment that the talks would affect the trial, currently in the jury selection process.
Kaye also said there could be constitutional problems with using a settlement agreement such as the tobacco pact being discussed to bar others from going to court.

Tobacco industry attorneys responded that the motion was an attempt by the Rosenblatts to gain attention in the media. Tobacco lawyers have repeatedly asked the judge to limit publicity about the case.
